subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Which owner boundary should drive the next step for this multi-agent Telegram/provider timeout report: live reproduction first, a targeted runtime/channel fix, or closing only after mitigation proof?
rationale: The evidence crosses Telegram runner concurrency, provider transport, model fallback, session/runtime timeouts, and launch defaults; choosing a code path before a current-main live trace could add the wrong fallback or config policy.

options.title: Run Current-Main Live Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a four-agent Telegram trace on current main before selecting a code or config change.

options.title: Split To A Broader Runtime Tracker
options.body: Treat this issue as a specific symptom and move remaining architecture work to a broader open Gateway/runtime pressure issue if maintainers decide that is the canonical owner.

options.title: Close After Positive Mitigation Proof
options.body: Only close this issue if a current-main run shows the original simultaneous timeout pattern no longer occurs after the merged fallback mitigations.

recommendation.title: Run Current-Main Live Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a four-agent Telegram trace on current main before selecting a code or config change.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent review and verification history across the fallback/gateway timeout path and is a good routing owner for the cross-surface decision.
